segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I had us down to talk through the 42-seat rollout for the operations team and make sure the May 6 go-live still works.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s right. We’re at 38 users today, but I want the agreement written for 42 so I’m not coming back in June for four more seats.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Makes sense. At 42 seats on the annual plan, it’s $31,080 for the year, and the standard onboarding package is $3,500 one-time. So first-year total is $34,580 before tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And payment terms are net 30? Our finance team cuts checks on the 15th and the last business day.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, net 30 is fine. If we get signature by April 19, the invoice would go out the next business day, so it should line up cleanly with your end-of-month run.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. The other thing is contract length. We don’t want auto-renew for more than a year. Legal is pretty firm on that.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. We can do a one-year initial term with annual renewals, and a 30-day notice window if you don’t want to renew. That’s in our standard terms.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. For go-live, we need the admin training the week of April 29. Our warehouse supervisors are in town Tuesday through Thursday only.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Okay, then I’ll include admin training on April 30 at 11 a.m. Central and end-user enablement on May 2. That gives us a few days before May 6 for permissions and testing.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. Send me the order form with those dates and the 42 seats. I’ll route it to procurement today.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it over this afternoon, and I’ll include the billing contact as finance@northlakeparts.com unless you want a different address.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: No, that’s the right one. Thanks, Mark.
